page: Google Cloud Platform c3-highmem-8 is an x86_64 server instance optimized for memory-intensive workloads within the C3 general architecture. It provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating an Intel Xeon 8481C processor clocked at 2.7 GHz. The compute architecture features a large 105 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, supplemented by advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware cryptography (AES, VAES, SHA-NI). Memory capacity is fixed at 64 GB, offering an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB per vCPU. The server does not bundle local storage, hardware accelerators, or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations position the c3-highmem-8 firmly within the middle tier across compute and memory operations. The instance achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 6,586.0 and a single-core score of 1,706.0, aligned with a PassMark CPU score of 11,819.82. Memory subsystems delivered 544.59 GB/sec in small-block cached read throughput, alongside 51.18 GB/sec read and 32.03 GB/sec write bandwidth on large 256 MB blocks. Memory operations register consistently in the mid-range, facilitating 8.86 million Redis SET operations per second and a PassMark database operations metric of 4,055.25. Decompression under multi-threaded bzip3 and larger model LLM token generation (7.34 tokens/sec on a 7B model) demonstrate weak relative performance, showing constraints when saturated across heavy parallel execution.

Cost efficiency is supported by dedicated resource isolation alongside a generous memory footprint, removing resource contention risks common to burstable tiers. The absence of attached local NVMe drives requires reliance on persistent network storage, introducing external throughput overheads that should be factored into overall architecture design. The instance is suited for in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, medium-scale relational databases, and enterprise data processing pipelines requiring high RAM allocations relative to raw core counts.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3-highmem-8 is an x86_64 instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor clocked at 2.7 GHz. Equipped with 64 GB of system memory, it delivers an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation designed for memory-demanding tasks. The processor incorporates 105 MB of L3 cache along with AVX-512 and AMX instruction extensions. The configuration lacks attached local disks, GPUs, and complimentary public IPv4 networking. Performance benchmarks across Geekbench, PassMark, and stress-ng place the instance consistently within average tiers, demonstrated by 8.86 million Redis SET operations per second and 51.18 GB/sec large-block read throughput. Relative performance lowers during multi-threaded decompression and larger LLM generation tasks. Given the memory-rich profile and reliance on networked storage, c3-highmem-8 is suited for in-memory key-value stores, caching infrastructure, and database operations.
